previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent UTIs and COPD, was admitted for treatment of a complicated urinary tract infection caused by cefepime-sensitive Klebsiella pneumoniae. She presented with urinary incontinence and had a history of frequent catheterization. IV cefepime was initiated via her existing PICC line, and her leukocytosis improved during the hospital stay. A chest CT revealed new right basilar consolidation, likely due to chronic aspiration given her neuromuscular impairment and patulous esophagus, but she remained afebrile and asymptomatic, so no additional treatment was initiated. She was managed for acute shoulder pain from a recent non-displaced scapular fracture with oxycodone and lidocaine patches. She was discharged home with services to complete a 7-day course of IV antibiotics, ongoing oxygen at 2L, and follow-up plans for pulmonary and swallow evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with paraplegia ___ s/p traumatic fall, with h/o 
recurrent ESBL UTIs and pneumonias, COPD, presenting with 
hypoxia and hypotension.

ACTIVE ISSUES: 

#) Hypotension: At admission to the ICU the patient's 
hypotension was most concerning for septic shock given history 
of recurrent urinary and pulmonary infection. Her u/a was 
concerning for infection and she had a new O2 requirement, which 
was concerning for possible urinary or pulmonary source. 
Additionally, the patient was not taking a lot of po's for 
several days prior to admission, so dehydration may have been 
contributing to her hypotension. There was also concern that the 
patient has underlying autonomic dysfunction since she is known 
to have low baseline blood pressures. In the ICU she required 
low doses of levophed to maintain stable blood pressures and 
MAP>60.  She was empirically treated for pneumonia or a UTI with 
vanc/cefepime/azithromycin.

#) Hypoxemia due to HCAP and acute diastolic CHF: The patient 
has a history of spinal cord injury and restrictive lung disease 
on 2 liters home oxygen. The hypoxemia was likely multifactorial 
due to pneumonia and pulmonary edema as her CT showed severe 
pulmonary edema superimposed on right upper lobe pneumonia in 
addition to stable right lower lobe dense consolidation. Given 
her underlying lung disease and recurrent pneumonia she was 
treated with broad spectrum antibiotics covering MDR organisms 
with vancomycin, cefepime, and azithromycin and completed an day 
course. With increased sputum production and increased O2 
requirement with wheezing on exam she was also treated for a 
COPD exacerbation with standing nebulizer treatments and a short 
course of prednisone. For the acute diastolic heart failure she 
was given IV lasix with symptomatic improvement. She was not 
continued on lasix on discharge. A TTE was performed that showed 
an EF >55% with higher pulmonary artery pressures and dilated RV 
compared to prior. 

#) UTI: The patient has a h/o multiple ESBL klebsiella UTIs 
which have been sensitive to cefepime and carbapenem.  Her urine 
culture on admission grew drug resistant Proteus and 
Enterococcus. She was treated with a 10 day course of cefepime 
and vancomycin.  Per outpatient infectious disease notes of Dr. 
___, the plan was to check for fosfomycin 
sensitivities and treat/prophylax with fosfomycin in the case of 
future UTIs. Fosphomycin sensitivities were added on to ___ 
urine culture - zone size was 7mm (Zone size determined using a 
method that has not been standardized for this drug- organism 
combination and for which no CLSI or FDA-approved interpretative 
standards exist. Interpret results with caution). 
- A repeat UA/UCx was checked prior to d/c (WBC 9 down from 118, 
leuks small, UCx NGTD).
.
CHRONIC ISSUES:

#) Anxiety/depression: Stable continued on home dose of 
citalopram. Clonazepam at low dose as needed for anxiety was 
avoided in the setting of low blood pressures, while she was in 
the ICU.

#) Spastic paraplegia: Stable. Continued home dose of baclofen.

#) Chronic pain: Stable. Continued home regimen of lidocaine 
patches, gabapentin, lyrica, and topamax. 
 
#) Neurogenic bladder: She was not on any medications for 
incontinence/spastic bladder at admission. While in the ICU she 
had a foley in place which was continued on the floor for urine 
output monitoring. Her foley was subsequently discontinued.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Cough and increased oxygen requirements.

COMPARISON:  CT chest ___.  Chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  Upright AP image of the chest was obtained.  A right basilar
opacity likely reflects chronic consolidation.  There is possible minimal
diffuse bilateral interstitial edema.  There are emphysematous changes.  There
is cardiomegaly.  A PICC line entering via a right subclavian vein appears to
end in the low superior vena cava.  There is left upper arm hardware device.  

IMPRESSION:  Minimal pulmonary interstitial edema.  Stable cardiomegaly. 
Chronic consolidation in the right lung base.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with paraplegia and recurrent pneumonias,COPD
now with increased oxygen requirement and hypotension.

COMPARISON:  CT chest, ___

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT imaging of the chest was obtained without
intravenous contrast.  Axial reformations at 1.25- and 5-mm slice thickness
were reviewed in conjunction with multiplanar reformations.

FINDINGS:  New multifocal ground-glass opacities in both lungs, predominant in
the upper lobes with smooth septal thickening, are most suggestive of severe
pulmonary edema.  Additional more consolidative opacities in the right upper
lobe (3:19) represent superimposed pneumonia.  Dense consolidation involving
major part of the right lower lobe with air bronchograms stable since
___, likely atelectasis may relate to diaphragmatic dysfunction.  Trace
right pleural effusion and pericardial effusion are stable.  Cardiomegaly,
predominantly involving the right atrium with a relatively normal sized right
ventricle, is unchanged.  The main pulmonary artery is enlarged measuring 35
mm, consistent with pulmonary arterial hypertension.  The thoracic aorta is
unremarkable. Few borderline enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes including a 9-mm
right upper paratracheal (2:11) and prevascular lymph nodes (2:22) are stable
since the prior study, so is a calcified 13-mm left infrahilar lymph node.  A
fluid density lesion in the azygoesophageal recess (2:32), less well seen in
this non-contrast study, appears similar to the prior studies, and may
represent a pericardial recess or bronchopulmonary foregut cyst.  

This study is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic assessment, however limited
imaging of the upper abdomen is unremarkable.

BONES:  Multiple bilateral old healed rib fractures are seen.  No bone lesions
suspicious for infection or malignancy are detected.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Severe pulmonary edema, with likely superimposed right upper lobe
pneumonia. Reactive mediastinal nodes.
2.  Stable right lower lobe dense consolidation, likely atelectasis due to
diaphragmatic dysfunction.
3.  Stable fluid density right azygoesophageal recess lesion, likely a
pericardial recess or bronchopulmonary foregut cyst.  

The above findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 10:40 a.m. on
___.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with COPD, on oxygen, admitted for pneumonia and
pulmonary edema.  Question change.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Substantial increase in the severity of consolidation in both mid and lower
lung zones, particularly the right, could be due to worsening of either edema
or bilateral pneumonia.  Severe cardiomegaly and at least a small if not
larger right pleural effusion are chronic.  Multiple rib fractures are seen in
various stages of healing on both sides of the chest.

SINGLE FRONTAL VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Worsening dyspnea, pulmonary edema, COPD and probably
pneumonia.

Comparison is made with prior study ___.

Extensive bilateral lung opacities larger on the right side are stable. 
Cardiomegaly and widened mediastinum are unchanged.  Right central catheter
tip is at the cavoatrial junction.  There is no pneumothorax.  Small bilateral
pleural effusions larger on the right side are probably unchanged.  Multiple
bilateral rib fractures are again noted.

AP CHEST, 10:45 A.M., ___  

HISTORY:  ___ woman with spinal cord injury and restrictive lung
disease.  Bronchiectasis and home oxygen.  Admitted with dyspnea, being
treated for pneumonia and pulmonary edema.

IMPRESSION:  PA and lateral chest compared to ___:

There has been substantial improvement in asymmetric pulmonary consolidation
suggesting that it is probably largely pulmonary edema in the upper lungs. 
The right lower lobe is clearing a region of consolidation much more slowly,
and this might be a pneumonia responding to treatment.  Small right pleural
effusion is stable.  There is no appreciable pleural effusion on the left. 
Severe cardiomegaly is chronic.  There are multiple bilateral rib fractures in
various stages of healing, but no pneumothorax.  Right jugular line ends low
in the SVC.
